author: GamingBolt
description:
Onimusha fans have been waiting for the series to awaken from its long slumber for a long time, and Way of the Sword sees the franchise do just that in impressive fashion. 

Though there’s obviously no dearth of options out there for fans of swordfighting action games, it wouldn’t be an exaggeration to call Onimusha’s comeback one of the best of all of those options. If complex, satisfying, mechanically tight combat is what you’re looking for, look no further than Onimusha: Way of the Sword.
title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword Review - An Absolutely Fantastic Comeback

author: GamingBolt
description:
Sometimes, The Blood of Dawnwalker's ambitions don’t always work. The world can feel strangely indifferent to Coen’s vampiric form, vertical traversal lacks polish, and combat progression, with its inherent skill trees, feels slow to blossom. 

And, furthermore, some activities regress into familiar open-world busywork, despite the narrative developments. Yet, none of these shortcomings stopped me from wanting to discover what happens next. For all its rough edges, The Blood of Dawnwalker has given me something incredibly rare: a reason to care about the consequences of inaction.
title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Review - One of the Best RPGs of 2026

author: GamingBolt
description:
Has it really been more than 11 years since the last true XCOM game (and no, Chimera Squad doesn't count)? We've seen plenty of notable standouts that put their own unique spins on the formula, from the Mario + Rabbids games to Troubleshooter. While they're certainly enjoyable in their own right, I've been left wanting for a title that really channels that XCOM feel. 

And not just a facsimile, but also something that really evolves on the formula in ways that make sense. Heck, throw some Star Wars in by way of The Clone Wars as well because why not? You wouldn't think Bit Reactor could pull that off with Star Wars Zero Company, and yet, to use a cliché, it's scratching that XCOM itch like so few other titles have over the years.
title: Star Wars Zero Company Review - A Deeply Satisfying Experience
